I've lived in Brazil for 6 months, so I do know what I talk about when it comes to churrascos.
And I can tell you that Au Lac do Brazil is a wonderful place both for the ones who miss churrasco and the ones curious to try (and as well for the ones willing to impress their guests, be it for a business meeting or a date)
As a typical Brazilian churrasco, you get plenty of kind of meat, offered at your table.

I got the chance to talk to the owners, nice people, and when you learn the story of the creation, them discovering churrasco while in Portugal, loving it and deciding to import it to Vietnam, with a Brazilian chef coming for a few weeks to teach them all the ins and out, you understand why this is a must go..

Heaven for a Carnivore!!
Jul 2017 • Friends
All you carnivores out there must try out this restaurant! You will leave the place with a smile on your face and your tummy in your hands!! 

The meats were of very good quality, and cooked beautifully preserving the juiciness of the different kinds of meat. Actually everything that came out of the kitchen to our table was just heavenly!

One word of advice - do pace yourself and not be greedy with the first few dishes e.g. the breads and rice, because what follow are even more delicious! 

The ambience inside the restaurant is quite good, but you'll be too busy with the food to pay much attention. There is a lone guitarist to croon a few songs while you eat, and again, he is fighting a losing battle .... all attention on .... food!

If you are not on a budget, then do go and spoil yourself. Our bill, food and alcohol, for 9 people came to about US$60 per head, not including tips! It was worth it!!

Its top quality ingredients , variety of dishes ( there is even an a la carte menu for vegetarians or small appetites), and above all CONSISTENCY ,make Au Lac do Brazil come in my top 3 venues in Vietnam list every year without fail, and I first arrived in Saigon in 1994.
 But there is also the atmosphere! 
 For all the above reasons Au Lac is a very significant venue for not only a quiet private evening in contemplation, ( I once dined alone at the equally brilliant Hanoi venue ), but also for family nights out, parties and for company or business entertaining.
 I think the many existing reviews have described the food and standards of hospitality but I should like to add that Au lac is my preferred restaurant for parties, amongst so many able competitors, for three reasons:

 1) The guests always find something they like to eat, more often everything.
 2) Ordering the Churaschuria ( still can't spell it!), saves so much time, dispute and disappointment.
 3) Above all, and I admit it's rather selfish , it's a very rare venue in that the host can fully enjoy the party and attend to the guests, without having to ensure that everything runs smoothly.
 I have not been to a restaurant in Vietnam where I have had to shout out "Em oi!" so rarely.
 

 Pricing? It features heavily in previous reviews and rightly so . The problem is that pricing and perceived value is so subjective and therefore opinions differ. The consensus view that I receive from Saigon resident expats like myself is that it continues to offer very good value for money despite the continually rising costs of the imported food stuffs. For pre-arranged big parties it's surely better than that.
 I know that I certainly got a really good price on one big party I arranged there, because I could compare it against the tenders from other operators competing for the occasion.

 Lastly, I forgot to mention the house wines : Chilean Chardonnay and Cab Sav. A great deal of thought went into the selection of these and I usually drink them. However, I should guess that the owners would have no objections if you decided to order a more prestigious wine from their impressive list!
